back2basics.text: Decent work means employment that provides fair income, workplace rights, social security, and dignity. It is a concept promoted by the International Labour Organization and is part of the Sustainable Development Goals. Decent work ensures that employment contributes to economic security and social inclusion, beyond just having a job.

back2basics.text: Coal mining is a major source of energy in India, supplying fuel primarily to thermal power plants. Production and supply depend on factors like mining capacity, transportation infrastructure, and seasonal weather conditions such as monsoons which can disrupt operations. body.label: Three major operations
body.text: The CBN Madhya Pradesh Unit conducted three significant operations in late October 2026, seizing a total of 2,774.650 kg of illicit poppy straw and five vehicles.

body.label: Largest seizure details
body.text: On 27 October, a Rajasthan-registered container truck was intercepted on the Mumbai–Delhi Expressway near Sitamau carrying 2,308 kg of poppy straw concealed under chana husk sacks; one person was arrested.

body.label: Second operation details
body.text: On the night of 28-29 October, a Mahindra pickup truck and a Mahindra Bolero car were intercepted in Mandsaur district, recovering 416.560 kg of poppy straw; one person was arrested and another fled.

body.label: Third operation details
body.text: On 28 October, a Hyundai Grand i10 car and a TVS motorcycle were stopped on the Fatehgarh–Nayakheda–Pipliya Mandi route, recovering 50.090 kg of poppy straw; two persons were arrested.

body.label: Arrests and network scope
body.text: The ED arrested four accused, including a Myanmar national, linked to an international narco-hawala network involved in drug trafficking and money laundering.

body.label: Key persons and roles
body.text: Chintuang, a Myanmar-based supplier, was linked to a 49.1 kg methamphetamine seizure in August 2025; Lalrammuana was the main handler; Jabrul Haque the receiver at the Damchhera-Kanhmun border; Abu Saleh operated accounts receiving ₹11.44 crore.

body.label: Hawala operations and transactions
body.text: The network converted Indian currency into Myanmarese Kyat at daily rates of about 42 to 48 Kyat per Rupee, with individual transactions up to ₹54.47 lakh a day and cumulative transactions exceeding 43 crore Kyat.

body.label: Use of drug money
body.text: Drug money was converted into ordinary goods like flour, edible oil, fuel, groceries, medicines, footwear, and cloth, which were sent to Myanmar, masking the illicit funds.

body.label: Asset seizures
body.text: Cash books, registers, handwritten accounts, seven signed ₹10 notes used as payment tokens, an immovable property purchased for ₹60 lakh, and 991 bank accounts linked to the network were seized or frozen.

back2basics.text: The Chief of Air Staff is the professional head of the Indian Air Force responsible for operational readiness, strategic planning, and modernization. The Air Force continuously adapts to technological and geopolitical changes by upgrading platforms, enhancing indigenous capabilities, and fostering jointness with other services to maintain national security.

2026-11-02-am-e761fb0f6b.deck: On 1 November 2026, Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit took charge as the 29th Chief of the Indian Air Force and outlined his strategic vision ‘VAYU’ focusing on operational readiness, self-reliance, innovation, and jointness. This leadership change and vision are important for understanding the future trajectory of India's air defence capabilities and modernization efforts.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit and the ‘VAYU’ vision:
1. He assumed charge as the 29th Chief of Air Staff on 1 November 2026 and has over 3,500 hours of flying experience.
2. The ‘VAYU’ vision includes pillars of Vigilance, Aatmanirbharta, Yukti, and Unity of Effort focused on operational readiness, indigenous capability, innovation, and jointness.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
mcq.trap: A trap could be confusing the number of flying hours or the pillars of the ‘VAYU’ vision; both statements are correct as per the evidence.

body.label: Profile and experience
body.text: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit is an Experimental Test Pilot and Qualified Flying Instructor with over 3,500 flying hours, having held key operational and strategic roles including Chief of Integrated Defence Staff and Vice Chief of the Air Staff.

body.label: Ceremonial assumption of charge
body.text: He assumed office on 1 November 2026, paying homage at the National War Memorial and receiving a ceremonial Guard of Honour at Air Force Station New Delhi.

sections.heading: Who is Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit and what is his background?

body.label: V - Vigilance, Victory and Readiness
body.text: Focus on maintaining the highest operational preparedness across all formations and restoring the IAF's combat strength to sanctioned levels.

body.label: A - Aatmanirbharta (Self-reliance)
body.text: Accelerating indigenous development of platforms, sensors, weapons, and technologies to ensure operational self-reliance and sustained combat capability.

body.label: Y - Yukti (Ingenuity and Innovation)
body.text: Harnessing innovation in doctrine, technology, and operations including AI-enabled command and control, counter-drone capabilities, and emerging operational domains.

body.label: U - Unity of Effort
body.text: Strengthening jointness with the Army, Navy, and national agencies aligned with the national vision of Jointness, Aatmanirbharta, and Innovation.

sections.heading: What is the ‘VAYU’ vision outlined by the new Chief of Air Staff?

body.label: Adapting to evolving warfare
body.text: The vision addresses the changing character of warfare shaped by drones, long-range precision weapons, space, cyber, AI, and electromagnetic spectrum.

body.label: Focus on indigenous capabilities
body.text: Prioritising indigenous platforms like Tejas Mk1A and Mk2, Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA), and Indian sensors and weapons to reduce dependence on foreign technology.

body.label: Enhancing joint operations
body.text: Emphasising integrated planning and operations with other armed forces and agencies to maximise air power effectiveness.

body.label: Personnel welfare and morale
body.text: Commitment to the training, professional excellence, morale, safety, and welfare of Air Warriors, Agniveervayu, civilian employees, veterans, and their families.
